name: 24LC256
full_name: Microchip 24LC256 256Kbit (32K x 8) I2C CMOS Serial EEPROM
description: The 24LC256 is a 256 Kbit (32,768 x 8) electrically erasable PROM with a two-wire I2C interface. It operates from 2.5V to 5.5V and supports 100 kHz and 400 kHz bus speeds, with a 64-byte page write buffer and a self-timed 5 ms write cycle. Three address pins (A0-A2) let up to eight devices share one bus at addresses 0x50-0x57. Rated for over one million erase/write cycles and more than 200 years data retention. Its standout trait is being the de facto hobbyist I2C EEPROM, pin-compatible across the entire 24xx serial family.

pins.name: A0
pins.description: user-configurable chip address bit 0, sets I2C slave address LSB

pins.name: A2
pins.description: user-configurable chip address bit 2, address 0b1010 A2 A1 A0 (0x50-0x57)

pins.name: WP
pins.description: write protect; high = read-only, low or floating = writes enabled

typical_application: Nonvolatile storage of configuration, calibration, or logging data for microcontrollers over I2C.
gotchas: SDA and SCL are open-drain and require external pull-up resistors (typically 4.7k-10k)
WP left floating does not guarantee write-enable on all clones; tie it to VSS to be sure writes work
address byte is 0b1010 A2 A1 A0, so only eight devices per bus; tie unused A pins, do not leave floating
page writes wrap within the 64-byte page boundary; crossing it overwrites the start of the same page
poll for ACK (acknowledge polling) after a write; the device is busy for up to 5 ms and will NAK during that time
do not confuse with 24LC256 vs 24AA256 (1.7V) vs 24FC256 (1 MHz) variants when buying for a fixed-voltage rail
